title: The Morning Brief: CTE research, FIFA fractures, racing probe, transfer moves
dek: Matt Hasselbeck joined a living-diagnosis study for chronic traumatic encephalopathy as African football's unified backing of Gianni Infantino fractured for the first time. Horse racing integrity officials launched investigations into five races after unusual betting and form reversals, while transfer activity accelerated across European soccer and the NFL's preseason took shape.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Hasselbeck's participation in CTE research marks a step toward the first living diagnosis of a disease confirmed in over 100 deceased NFL players; Isha Johansen's public call for Infantino to resign breaks the African continental consensus that has shielded him since the FIFA Forward Enterprise collapse; and integrity investigators are examining five horse races from Sunday after overseas bookmakers flagged anomalies for the first time.
bottom_line: Hasselbeck's participation advances CTE research toward a living diagnosis that remains years away. Johansen's public break from African backing marks the first prominent continental voice against Infantino, though CAF leadership remains officially unified. Horse racing integrity officials are investigating five races after overseas bookmakers flagged betting and form anomalies for the first time. Watson returns to live action Saturday after missing the entire 2025 season. Watch for HISA's post-race drug-test results and findings, whether other African football leaders follow Johansen's lead, and whether Watson can execute extended drives in his first game since October 2024.
body: Matt Hasselbeck, the 50-year-old former three-time Pro Bowl quarterback, spent two days at Boston University undergoing brain scans, blood tests, and cognitive assessments as part of a multi-site study funded by a $15 million National Institutes of Health award in 2025. The work targets the gap that defines modern CTE research: the disease has been confirmed in more than 100 deceased NFL players, yet doctors have no method to diagnose it in a living patient. Hasselbeck's 17-year NFL career with Green Bay, Seattle, Tennessee, and Indianapolis, coupled with three pre-college concussions he can account for and an unknown number during his playing years, makes him a critical baseline volunteer. He is committing to donate his brain for autopsy research after his death. The research is foundational and early; small enrollment across all sites means years may pass before a living CTE diagnostic test reaches clinical use.

In soccer governance, Isha Johansen, a former FIFA Council member and former Sierra Leone Football Association president, publicly called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign, citing ethical breaches in the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and a breakdown of trust in his leadership. Johansen's intervention carries particular symbolic weight: in 2021, when she stepped down from the SLFA presidency three months after her March 2021 FIFA Council election, Infantino personally visited Sierra Leone with CAF president Patrice Motsepe and advised her to resign "for the good of football." She is now invoking that same language against him. Her statement breaks the unified African backing that has insulated Infantino from continental pressure; the Confederation of African Football's executive committee has unanimously supported him and his 2027 re-election bid, while UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation have formally accused him of deception over the FIFA Forward Enterprise. Johansen frames the European confederations' dissent as justified and says CAF's swift backing of Infantino risks reinforcing the perception that African football prioritizes FIFA money over ethical governance.

Horseracing integrity officials opened investigations into five races held Sunday at Saratoga Race Course and Monmouth Park after detecting unusual betting patterns and dramatic performance improvements on horses linked to Fair Hill Training Facility in Maryland. The Great Amira, listed at 20-1 in the morning line, went off at 17-1 and won its race by 9.5 lengths despite finishing last in both lifetime starts. Tepeyac, 9-2 in the morning line, went off at 4-1 and won. Classic Rock was 10-1 in the morning line, went off at 8-1, and won by 8.75 lengths. M B Melanie Cares went off at 12-1 and won by over three lengths. Only Scootaloo finished out of the money. The investigation was triggered by alerts from U.S. and U.K. bookmakers, marking the first time overseas betting operators have flagged anomalies in American racing to the Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority.

In soccer transfers, Inter Milan advanced negotiations with Tottenham over a deal for full-back Djed Spence worth a minimum of 25.6 million pounds, though no agreement has been finalized. Spence, 26, enhanced his profile at the World Cup with eight appearances for England and is available as Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi does not view him as essential. Manchester City completed the signing of Argentina goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille on a two-year contract; BBC Sport reported the fee as 1.7 million pounds, while ESPN reported it at 1.75 million euros fixed of up to 2 million euros total. Rulli, 34, returns to the club where he spent 2016-17 without making a first-team appearance and will serve as backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma. The signing fills the void left by James Trafford's departure to Leeds on a deal worth up to 45 million pounds.

In the NFL, the Cleveland Browns named Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback for Saturday's preseason opener against Chicago. Watson will play his first game since tearing his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and undergoing a second Achilles surgery in January 2025, missing the entire 2025 season. Shedeur Sanders will start the Browns' second preseason game at home against Buffalo on August 22. Browns coach Todd Monken informed the quarterbacks of his decision after practice Wednesday.
